title: Chapter 140 — On-Site Damage Discovery
intro: The delivery crew opens the box and there is a dent.

sections.title: The On-Site Protocol
sections.content:
Stop. Document with photos from all angles. Call the store before the crew leaves. Give the customer immediate options: refuse delivery and reschedule with a perfect unit, accept with a documented damage claim for compensation, or accept a floor model at a discount if one is available.

Never let the crew leave without a decision and documentation. Once they drive away, the damage becomes a he-said-she-said situation that is 10 times harder to resolve.

sections.title: The Customer Response
sections.content: '[Name], I am so sorry. A dent on a brand new refrigerator is unacceptable. Here is what I am going to do right now. Can you send me a photo? I am filing the damage claim immediately — you will not have to deal with that paperwork. And I have two options for you: replacement delivery at the earliest slot, or if the damage is cosmetic and you would rather keep it, I can offer you a $[X] accommodation. Which would you prefer?'

sections.title: Preventing Recurrence
sections.content:
After every damage incident, trace it back. Was it damaged in transit? Was it damaged in the warehouse? Was it damaged during unboxing? Each root cause has a different fix.

Document every incident. Patterns tell you whether you have a carrier problem, a warehouse handling problem, or a packaging problem. One dent is an incident. Three dents on the same route is a systemic issue.
